newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: INSTANT VIEW - S&P ups Argentina long-term debt.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - S&P ups Argentina long-term debt.

text.p: The following is a selection of economists' and analysts' initial reactions to Standard & Poor's upgrade of Argentina's long-term foreign currency debt rating to BB from BB-.
ROBERTO COSTA BOURDIEU, SENIOR FIXED INCOME ANALYST, BANCO RIO DE LA PLATA
"This is great news considering the fears over the U.S. Federal Reserve and the long U.S. bond.
"This could make a difference for investors. Maybe there will be reduction of 40 basis points in the spread to Mexican par bonds."
JOSE RUTMAN, ECONOMIST AT CONSULTANTS BRODA Y ASOCIADOS
"This is good news for Argentina. It confirms what we were expecting. We are still far from investment grade, we are missing two grades.
"Still we are now at the same level with S&P as that of Duff & Phelps for Argentina. I would not rule out that D&P raises its rating as well."
RAUL BUONUOME, ARGENTINE ECONOMIST AT DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL.
"This upgrade by one rating puts us aside Mexico which is also BB. It is recognition of the efforts by Argentina to improve the credibility of the country with investors."
"This will reduce country risk by 50 to 60 basis points at least. I was surprised they did not change the outlook and maintained it at stable."
ESTEBAN THOMSEN, ARGENTINA ECONOMIST AT ING BARINGS.
"There was not much of a consensus that they were going to raise the rating all the way to BB, so therefore this is generating a good reaction.
"There is a world of investors with investment rules that could not invest in Argentina. Therefore now there is a new group of investors that can invest here."
